newsitem.title: ITALY: Mediaset sees debt eliminated by year-end.
newsitem.headline: Mediaset sees debt eliminated by year-end.

text.p: Italian television and advertising group Mediaset expects to eliminate its net financial debts by the end of 1996 from 285 billion lire at the end of June this year, chairman Fedele Confalonieri said.

Confalonieri, speaking in the sidelines of a convention here, said in the first 10 months of the year business of Publitalia, Mediaset's advertising arm which accounts for 90 percent of its turnover, grew 6.5 percent.
This was a growth rate which "we expect to maintain until the end of the year," Confalonieri said.
In October the advertising agency registered a record monthly turnover of 377 billion lire, equal to an annual growth rate of 30 percent.
September also showed an increase of 16 percent, he said.
In the first six months of the year, Mediaset's consolidated turnover was 1.675 billion lire with a pretax profit of 497.4 billion lire.

Confalonieri also said if Mediaset did not have the chance to compete for a possible third license to manage a PCN standard mobile telephone service in Italy, it did not rule out interest in second license holder Omnitel or state controlled telecoms holding Stet whose privatisation is now expected in late 1997.
"Omnitel would be one of the opportunities we might consider but that would be considered at the time," he said.

Asked if in that case the only route would be to take a stake in Omnitel's largest shareholder Olivetti, he replied this was true but immediately added there had not been any talks with Olivetti's largest shareholder Carlo De Benedetti.

"Then there's also the privatisation of Stet," he added. "But it's all fluid, the only certainty is that in the future there will be convergence between television, telecommunications and information," he said.
